clue.text: Horace works when over in Black Sea location

parts.note: the Roman poet Horace is famed for his Odes

indicators.note: in a down-turned or backward sense, over says the word for when is turned round

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: A request to find where a poet's works stand when finished, somewhere on the Black Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horace works' is a whole phrase for one piece; 'over' is the down-style turnaround signal used here in an across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ukrainian port city lies on the north-western coast of the Black Sea.

clue.text: Hard-hearted alumnus expected to harbour traitor

parts.note: OB is short for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: to harbour is to give shelter within, so one word holds the other

parts.note: something expected is due
a rat is a betrayer or informer

explanation.surface: A cold former pupil is expected to give shelter to a betrayer.
explanation.walkthrough: OB (old boy) is the British term for a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Obdurate describes someone stubbornly unmoved, a close synonym of hard-hearted.

clue.text: Plug stops leak in daring exploit

indicators.note: a stopper sits inside an opening, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: an escape of gas or water is a leak
a plug is a piece of publicity, an ad

explanation.surface: Sounds like plumbing: a plug blocks a leak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' looks like the plumber's bung but means an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is an adventurous or reckless exploit.

clue.text: King Henry's artificial language

parts.note: Elvis Presley is known as the King of rock and roll
H is the symbol for the henry, the SI unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Reads as a jibe that a Tudor king spoke in contrived terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Henry' wants to be one Tudor monarch, but splits into the singer and a unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien invented a family of constructed tongues for his elves, known collectively by this name.

clue.text: Good money Scotsman put in Post Office — key investment?

parts.note: the rand is the currency of South Africa

indicators.note: the Scotsman is placed inside the office abbreviation

parts.note: Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A man from Scotland deposits good money at the post office as an investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' is not a financial word: the instrument has many keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A costly concert instrument with a keyboard may be bought as an investment piece, hence the playful question mark.

clue.text: Shimmering stone mate put on ring

indicators.note: one piece is placed on next to the other in the answer

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O
a mate or friend is a pal

explanation.surface: A friend sets a shimmering gem on a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring letter O comes first, with PAL placed on after it.
explanation.definitionFit: This gemstone is prized for its iridescent play of colour.

clue.text: Sacred musician has witty bishop back

indicators.note: back says the word for witty is read from its end

parts.note: dry humour is understated wit
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A church composer is joined by a clever bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: William Byrd was a Tudor composer of masses and anthems; 'back' turns the whole of DRY plus B round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elizabethan composer wrote much church music, such as masses and motets.

clue.text: Argus, say, gutted swordfish with grip loosened

indicators.note: a gutted fish has its insides taken out, leaving only the outer letters
letters loosened from their order are shuffled into a new one

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fisherman guts a swordfish and slackens his hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loosened' rearranges WITH GRIP into IPWRIGHT. In Greek myth Argus built the ship Argo for Jason.
explanation.definitionFit: Argus was the legendary builder of the Argo, so he is an example of a boat-builder.

clue.text: One wanting to stop keeps writing to an author

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the other pieces go within

parts.note: a braker is one who applies the brakes, wanting to halt
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone eager to halt hangs on to letters addressed to a novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One wanting to stop' looks like a would-be quitter, but means someone hitting the brakes; 'keeps' puts the two shorter pieces inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish novelist wrote Dracula, so he is one example of a writer.

clue.text: Occident becomes Orient for this comedian

parts.note: the Occident is the West, abbreviated W
becomes in the sense of 'is' or 'equals'
the Orient is the East, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: A riddle of the West turning into the East for a comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernie Wise was half of Morecambe and Wise, a much-loved British comedy double act.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie Wise was a British comic, partner of Eric Morecambe.

clue.text: Cold beer first — one Guinness so handled

indicators.note: first says the beer word comes before the other

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A drinker orders a cold beer before a pint of Guinness.
explanation.walkthrough: Guinness is not the stout: Sir Alec Guinness was a famous British actor, so 'one Guinness' is a person called this.
explanation.definitionFit: The actor Sir Alec Guinness bore this first name, so a Guinness addressed so.

clue.text: Rye Estates may offer financial security

indicators.note: the letters given may yield or offer another arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Property in the town of Rye might give a comfortable financial footing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may offer' rearranges RYE ESTATES. Rye is a town in East Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Living on this idiomatic road means enjoying a comfortable, well-off life free of money worries.

clue.text: Secure gold in horse-drawn carriage

parts.note: to land something is to secure or win it
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Someone stashes gold safely in a carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' here only links wordplay and definition; it is not putting one thing inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled carriage with a folding top, drawn by horses.

clue.text: Spymaster in passage makes broadcast

indicators.note: in places the spymaster inside the word for passage

parts.note: transit is passage from one place to another
M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: A spy chief in transit sends out a broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmit a signal or programme is to send it out over the air.

clue.text: One profiting from summer weather and punch

definitions.meaning: one who makes hay while the sun shines, cutting and drying grass

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a farm worker drying grass in sunshine and a heavy swinging blow.

clue.text: Saw always cuts grass

indicators.note: one piece cuts into the other, going inside it

parts.note: to grass is to inform on someone, to sing
ay is an old word for ever or always

explanation.surface: A saw is always used to cut grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is not the tool but a proverb; 'grass' is British slang for informing.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old proverb or maxim, a traditional wise utterance.

clue.text: Apollyon maybe sacked city in desolate region that's endless

indicators.note: in places the city within the shortened region
endless means the final letter is taken off

parts.note: a desert is a desolate region
Troy was the city sacked by the Greeks

explanation.surface: A ruined city lies in a barren land without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's endless' cuts DESERT to DESER. Apollyon is the angel of the abyss in Revelation, whose name means the Destroyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollyon, the biblical angel of the bottomless pit, is named the Destroyer, so it exemplifies the word.

clue.text: Wrong about reservists — journalist shamed

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist is disgraced by a wrong concerning army reservists.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is the British part-time reserve army.
explanation.definitionFit: Stained here means tainted or dishonoured, as a reputation is.

clue.text: Commander edges away from infidel

indicators.note: the edges of the word are taken away, losing its first and last letters

parts.note: a pagan is a heathen, an infidel

explanation.surface: An officer slips away from an unbeliever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edges away' looks like movement but strips the ends from PAGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An aga was a military commander or chief officer in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Longer and shorter periods written up in last letter

indicators.note: in a down clue, written up means the letters run upward, in reverse

parts.note: an age is a long period and a mo is a short moment
mo is short for a moment, a brief period

explanation.surface: Periods of time are recorded in a final letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written up' reverses AGEMO.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Deism for two in Reformation that Luther fled

indicators.note: re-formation means forming again, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Religious ideas set out in the age of Luther.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformation' reads as the Protestant movement but signals re-forming DEISM FOR TWO.
explanation.definitionFit: Luther was summoned before the imperial assembly at Worms in 1521 and left secretly after refusing to recant.

clue.text: Olivia upset by rat's head in food parcels

indicators.note: a head is the top or first letter of the word
upset means overturned, mixing the letters up

explanation.surface: Olivia is upset by a rat getting into the food parcels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles the name, and the rat's head letter goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are small pasta squares stuffed with filling, like little parcels of food.

clue.text: Inventive sort decorates Lancastrian houses

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the letters sit within the words

explanation.surface: A creative person paints and decorates homes in Lancashire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like a noun but is a verb: decorates Lancastrian contains the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikola Tesla was a celebrated inventor in electrical engineering.

clue.text: Maybe pay with dollar to avoid duty

definitions.meaning: literally handing over a buck, a dollar, as payment
to shift responsibility on to someone else

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means shifting responsibility elsewhere, and literally reads as handing over a dollar.

clue.text: Topless material shows class

indicators.note: without its top means the first letter goes

parts.note: silk is a fabric or material

explanation.surface: A risque topless fabric shows breeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' looks racy but just removes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilk means sort or kind, as in 'people of that ilk'.

clue.text: Western female receives praise falsely

indicators.note: receives means takes inside, so the scrambled word goes within

parts.note: a hen is a female bird

indicators.note: falsely means wrongly arranged, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A woman takes insincere compliments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falsely' scrambles the praise, and 'receives' puts that inside the female bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesperian is a poetic word for western, from Hesperus, the evening star in the west.

clue.text: First man to go beneath rising river's surface

indicators.note: in a down clue going beneath means coming after
in a down clue rising means read upward, in reverse

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
Adam was the first man in Genesis

explanation.surface: The first man dives under a river's surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses CAM to MAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Macadam is a road surface of compacted broken stone.

clue.text: Lazy Hardy disheartened by his entire output?

parts.note: a writer's complete works are his whole output

indicators.note: without its heart means the middle letters go, leaving the outer ones

explanation.surface: A novelist depressed by everything he has written.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hardy is the novelist; 'disheartened' leaves HY.
explanation.definitionFit: Workshy means unwilling to work, idle or lazy.

clue.text: Priest going about left one to chew the cud

indicators.note: going about means surrounding, so the priest goes round the letter

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest

explanation.surface: A priest wanders around leaving someone to ponder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chew the cud' suggests pondering but means a ruminant.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American ruminant, so it chews the cud.

clue.text: Lecherous god for example runs to save time

indicators.note: to save means keep, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: say is used for for example
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A lustful deity runs to make time.
explanation.definitionFit: A satyr is a woodland deity of Greek myth, half goat and known for lust.

clue.text: Fool starts with absolutely stupid statement

indicators.note: starts means the opening letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: A fool begins with a completely stupid remark.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is a silly person, a common synonym for a fool.
